benefits.name: Nebraska Homestead Exemption for Disabled Veterans
benefits.description: Nebraska's Homestead Exemption program provides property tax relief to qualifying disabled veterans, including veterans totally disabled by a service-connected accident or illness, qualified totally disabled veterans or their surviving spouse, and veterans whose home was substantially contributed to by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (and their widow(er)s). Applicants must own and occupy the homestead from January 1 through August 15 and submit Form 458 (Nebraska Homestead Exemption Application) along with Form 458B (Certification of Disability) when first applying and in years ending in 0 or 5. Exact exemption percentages vary by category and are published annually in the Department of Revenue's Homestead Exemption Information Guide and Category Requirements Table.
benefits.value: Property tax exemption on homestead value (percentage varies by disability category, up to full exemption for 100% service-connected disabled veterans)

otherReqs: Honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge required
Must own and occupy the homestead January 1 through August 15
Form 458 and Form 458B (Certification of Disability from VA) required initially and in years ending in 0 or 5

application.agency: Nebraska Department of Revenue, Property Assessment Division
application.form: Form 458 (Homestead Exemption Application); Form 458B (Certification of Disability)
documentation: Proof of homestead ownership and occupancy

benefits.name: Disabled/Blind Veteran Motor Vehicle Tax & Fee Exemption
benefits.description: Effective January 1, 2026, Nebraska exempts one vehicle owned and used for personal transportation by a qualifying disabled or blind veteran from the state Motor Vehicle Tax and Motor Vehicle Fee (other taxes and fees, such as plate fees, sales tax, and wheel tax, still apply). Eligible veterans are those honorably separated from active duty with an established service-connected disability (including a 0% rating) under 5 U.S.C. § 2108, or those currently receiving compensation, disability retirement benefits, or a pension from the VA or military; blind veterans qualify if their sight is so defective as to seriously limit ordinary vocations and activities, as recognized by the VA. Veterans must first enroll in the NDVA Military & Veterans' Registry with documentation of disability rating or benefit receipt, then request the exemption during vehicle registration or renewal within 30 days of purchase or before the renewal month expires. The exemption renews automatically thereafter.
benefits.value: Exemption from Motor Vehicle Tax and Motor Vehicle Fee on one vehicle

otherReqs: Honorable separation from active duty with an established service-connected disability (including 0%), or currently receiving VA/military compensation, disability retirement, or pension
Must enroll in the NDVA Military & Veterans' Registry first
Exemption request must occur within 30 days of purchase or before the renewal month expires
Applies to only one vehicle

application.agency: Nebraska Department of Veterans' Affairs / County Treasurer
documentation: NDVA Military & Veterans' Registry enrollment with disability rating or benefit receipt documentation

benefits.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate
benefits.description: Nebraska issues a Disabled Veteran license plate to veterans with an honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge who are at least 10% service-connected disabled and enrolled in the Nebraska Veteran's Registry, for a vehicle titled in their name (or as a trust beneficiary). The standard alphanumeric Disabled Veteran plate carries no additional fee beyond regular registration taxes/fees. A personalized Disabled Veteran Message Plate costs $40 annually (initial and renewal), split 75% to the Veteran Cemetery Cash Fund and 25% to the DMV Cash Fund.
benefits.value: No additional fee for the standard alphanumeric plate; $40/year for a personalized message plate

otherReqs: Honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge
At least 10% service-connected disability rating
Must be enrolled in the Nebraska Veteran's Registry
Vehicle must be titled in the veteran's name or held as a trust beneficiary

documentation: VA benefit summary showing at least 10% service-connected disability

benefits.name: Disabled Veteran Lifetime Hunt/Fish/Fur Combo & Park Entry Permit
benefits.description: Nebraska residents who are 50% or more service-connected disabled, or who are 100% non-service-connected disabled and receive a VA pension, are eligible for a free (no-cost) lifetime Resident Disabled Veteran Hunt/Fish/Fur Combo and/or Park Entry Permit. The permit has no expiration date and remains valid as long as the individual remains a Nebraska resident and continues to meet the disability guidelines. Nebraska separately offers a $5 Veteran's Annual Small Game Hunt/Fish/Fur Harvest Permit (including all state stamps) to resident veterans age 64 and older, and a one-time $5 permit for residents recently returned from deployment.
benefits.value: Free lifetime hunting/fishing/fur-harvest and park entry permit for qualifying disabled veterans; $5 annual permit for veterans 64+

otherReqs: 50%+ service-connected disability, OR 100% non-service-connected disability with VA pension
Must remain a Nebraska resident to keep the permit valid
Age-64+ tier requires DD-214 or Veteran Indicator on Nebraska driver's license

documentation: VA disability rating or pension documentation

benefits.name: Waiver of Tuition Program for Dependents
benefits.description: Nebraska waives up to 100% of tuition charges and tuition-related fees at University of Nebraska campuses, Nebraska state colleges, and Nebraska community colleges for the spouse, surviving spouse, biological child, adopted child, or stepchild of a veteran whom the VA has determined to be 100% permanently and totally disabled as a result of military service, or who died after discharge from an injury or illness sustained while in service, or who was classified as missing in action or a prisoner of war during armed hostilities. The waiver covers one degree/diploma/certificate from a community college and one baccalaureate degree from a university or state college, but does not cover housing, food, parking, or books/materials. The dependent must be a Nebraska resident and meet the school's in-state residency requirements; eligibility for dependent children generally ends at age 26 (extendable for those who served on active duty between ages 18-26).
benefits.value: Up to 100% waiver of tuition and tuition-related fees for one degree/certificate

otherReqs: Veteran must be 100% permanently and totally disabled, or have died from a service-connected injury/illness after discharge, or have been MIA/POW
Dependent must be a Nebraska resident meeting in-state tuition residency requirements
Covers only one credential per dependent (community college degree/diploma/certificate, or one baccalaureate degree)
Dependent child eligibility generally ends at age 26

documentation: VA documentation of veteran's 100% permanent and total disability, service-connected death, or MIA/POW status
Proof of relationship to the veteran

benefits.name: State Employment Veterans' Preference
benefits.description: Nebraska adds 5 percentage points to a passing state civil-service exam score for qualifying veterans, with an additional 5 percentage points (10 total) for qualifying disabled veterans. Preference may also be claimed by the spouse of a 100% disabled veteran, the spouse of a veteran killed in the line of duty or who died of service-connected causes, or the spouse of a service member currently on active duty or discharged within the past 180 days. Applicants must submit Form DD-214 (preferably Member Copy 4) and, if applicable, proof of service-connected disability or proof of marriage.
benefits.value: 5 percentage points added to passing exam score for veterans; 10 total for disabled veterans

otherReqs: DD-214 (preferably Member Copy 4) required
Disabled veteran preference requires proof of service-connected disability
Spousal preference requires proof of marriage

application.agency: Nebraska Department of Administrative Services, State Personnel Division
documentation: Proof of marriage (if claiming spousal preference)

benefits.name: Nebraska Veterans' Homes
benefits.description: Nebraska operates four state veterans' homes — Eastern Nebraska Veterans' Home (Bellevue), Central Nebraska Veterans' Home (Kearney), Norfolk Veterans' Home (Norfolk), and Western Nebraska Veterans' Home (Scottsbluff) — providing assisted living, skilled nursing, memory care, physical/occupational/speech therapy, and hospice/palliative care. Eligible veterans must have served on active duty with an honorable or general discharge and have lived in Nebraska for at least two years during their lifetime; spouses, surviving spouses, and Gold Star parents/spouses are also eligible under similar residency requirements. Member contributions operate on an income/asset-based sliding scale ($0 to $5,549/month); veterans rated 70-100% service-connected may receive care at no cost. The homes are overseen by the Nebraska Department of Veterans' Affairs and the Veterans' Homes Board.
benefits.value: Assisted living, skilled nursing, and memory care at four state veterans homes; sliding-scale cost, free for 70-100% service-connected veterans

otherReqs: Honorable or general discharge from active duty
Lived in Nebraska for at least 2 years during their lifetime
Spouses, surviving spouses, and Gold Star parents/spouses also eligible under similar residency rules

application.agency: Nebraska Department of Veterans' Affairs / Veterans' Homes Board
documentation: DD-214 or proof of military service
